insights.insight: Crinkl has confirmed 90,989 cryptographically verified receipts representing $4.8M in cumulative GMV — deterministic purchase proof, not probabilistic inference. For brands evaluating cookieless alternatives, this is a live, growing panel of confirmed buyers, not modeled audiences.

The network is generating 375–398 verified receipts per day on a structural basis, with a consistent late-UTC burst window adding 113–129 receipts and $5,500–$6,090 GMV in a single 4-hour interval. Volume is patterned and repeatable, not spiky.

Grocery-supermarkets leads at 1,511 receipts and $65K GMV over 14 days, followed by restaurants-dining and retail-department-stores — the three categories that account for the majority of CPG and QSR brand spend. Gas-convenience adds a fourth high-frequency touchpoint.

Walmart (353 receipts), Kroger (155), Target (115), and Costco (131) are already above the public visibility threshold in the 14-day window — meaning competitor and category benchmarking at the brand level is becoming structurally possible within this dataset.

Three new brand-list entries in four days — McDonald's (first QSR), Lowe's (second home-improvement retailer), and H-E-B (Texas-dominant regional grocer) — signal the network is adding geographic and vertical coverage, not just deepening existing strongholds. Thirty category/metro cells are now active across 18 metro areas.

Seven-day GMV is $89,455 across 2,115 receipts; the 14-day figure of $223,938 implies a consistent weekly pace with no visible decay. Pre-rollover daily closes have cleared $101K in eight of the last fifteen completed days, suggesting the run rate is holding rather than plateauing.
